To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified several novel QTL and candidate genes for SCS that are likely to be associated with susceptibility to mastitis in dairy cattle.

we performed a GWAS to identify genetic locuses that are associated with somatic-cell score, a trait that is indicative of the susceptibility of a cow to mastitis, and that we identified a number of genetic locuses that may be involved in the susceptibility of a dairy cow to mastitis.

we identified several novel QTL regions for SCS and SCS-related mastitis traits, including a novel region on chromosome 6 that is associated with SCS and contains a Y RNA gene, and that this gene was expressed in multiple different mastitic cell types.

the identification of new QTL and candidate genes for mastitits susceptibility in dairy cattle.
identifying the genes underlying QTL associated with mastitis susceptibility in dairy cattle and this study has identified several novel QTL and candidate genes for future functional studies.
the identification and characterisation of QTL regions and candidate genes that may play important roles in the susceptibility of the bovine to mastitis.
